messages.subject: Creating a geom_cladelabel argument based on vectors of nodes and clade names
messages.subject_clean: Creating a geom_cladelabel argument based on vectors of nodes and clade names
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I am trying to figure out a way to automate plotting clade labels using the geom_cladelab function in ggtree. I know it is possible to do so in phytools using code like so:

```
library(tidyverse);library(ape);library(phytools);library(ggtree);library(curl)
rodent.tree<-read.nexus(curl("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaraptor1/mydata/main/engelmanData.tree")) d<-read.csv(curl("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaraptor1/mydata/main/traitdata.csv")) df<- full_join(rodent.tree, d, by = 'node')
# Loading data for consideration
```

```
nodes<-c(mrca(rodent.tree)["Pectinator_spekei","Cavia_porcellus"],
         mrca(rodent.tree)["Pedetes_capensis","Idiurus_macrotis"],
         mrca(rodent.tree)["Sciurus_niger","Glis_glis"],
         mrca(rodent.tree)["Castor_canadensis","Thomomys_bottae"],
         mrca(rodent.tree)["Mus_musculus","Napaeozapus_insignis"])
labels<-c("Hystricomorpha","Anomaluromorpha","Sciuromorpha","Castorimorpha",
          "Myomorpha")
brain.fit<-fastAnc(rodent.tree,EQ,vars=TRUE,CI=TRUE)
obj<-contMap(rodent.tree,EQ,plot=FALSE)
plot(obj,type="fan",cex=5,fsize=.25,lwd=1.5)
for(i in 1:length(nodes))
  arc.cladelabels(text = labels[i],node = nodes[i],mark.node = TRUE,ln.offset =
                  1.23, col = c("green","red","cyan","orange","blue")[i], lab.offset =
                  1.27, fsize = .05, orientation = "curved")
```

However, I am trying to do the same in ggtree. Right now I have been calling separate geom_cladelab functions using mrca every time I plot the tree, which has been greatly increasing computation time as it has to return the number of each nodes, despite having a vector of node numbers and clade names. I tried plotting them using the aes argument in geom_cladelabel, but they did not work and returned the error message "argument "label" is missing, with no default".

```
ggtree(df,layout="circular",size=2.5)+
  geom_tree(aes(color=trait),continuous=T,size=2)+
  geom_tiplab(color="black",size=1,fontface='bold.italic')+
  geom_cladelabel(offset=20,aes(node=nodes,label=labels),color="red",hjust=1,align=T)+
  scale_color_gradientn(colours=c("red", 'orange', 'green', 'cyan', 'blue'))+
  geom_point2(aes(subset = (node %in% nodes)), color = "black",fill = c("cyan","green","red","blue","orange"), shape = 21, size = 8)
```

Trying the same call without having both in aes, or having nodes in aes and labels called manually, also returns an error.

I tried using the same solution proposed for calling a geom_point argument by node number here (https://groups.google.com/g/bioc-ggtree/c/pWS5hHmJFmA), but that also did not work for geom_cladlab. Is there any way to define geom_cladlab functions if the vectors of node number and clade name are known?

Sincerely,
Russell

messages.subject: Plot two trees to check congruency?
messages.subject_clean: Plot two trees to check congruency?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'd like to plot two trees with the same labels side by side to check to what extent they're congruent. An example of what I'd like to achieve: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3724504/figure/F3/?report=objectonly

I have tried the ggdensitree() function, but the result is messy, probably because clades and taxa are ordered differently in the two trees. I've looked through chapter 6 ("Visual exploration of phylogenetic tree") in the handbook but I fail to come up with a good strategy for how to loop through the two trees and ensure they are as similarly sorted as possible.

Does anyone have any ideas I could explore?

/D

And it is unclear to me where I would put scale_x_log10() if I wanted to have a custom scale for that facet.

Appreciate advice.

messages.body_plain:
As wonderful as ggtree() is, I have run into some limitations in combining different plot types using either geom_fruit() or facet_plot().

My solution is to simply combine the tree with a separate ggplot() panel using plot_grid().

But to do this correctly, I must order the taxa on the plot the same way they are ordered in the tree.  How can I find the order of the taxa in the tree so that I can use this order in a ggplot()?

Thanks,  Bill Pearson

The nodes i want to be coloured are called "n23", "n17", "n45".

For some analyses I had to manipulate the tree to become ultrametric using the chronos function in the package ape. Doing this changed my class from 'phylo' into 'chronos phylo'

> class(phy)
[1] "phylo"
> class(phy_ultra)
[1] "chronos" "phylo"

this doesn't seem to give any problems with further analyses of the tree in other packages, however, when I try to load my tree in with ggtree I get the following error

Error in UseMethod("as.phylo") :
  no applicable method for 'as.phylo' applied to an object of class "c('chronos', 'phylo')"

Is there a way to circumvent calling as.phylo()? Or is there another way to solve this?

Cheers
Pepijn

messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Yu,

I like the circular plot from the ggtree package very much.

I made NJ tree using the ape package and then plotted the tree with ape plot.phylo (type="fan") and ggtree circular layout, respectively. Personally, I like the ggtree circular plot better than fan plot with ape. I would like to color the edges of the tree according to groups. However, I found that ape and ggtree displayed clusters of the same NJ tree very differently. Because I started from the same NJ tree, I would expect the two plots should be identical to each other in terms of clusters and colors for each group.

I attached my code for both plots, could you please give me some hints on what's wrong with it? If possible, could you please correct my code for ggplot? (I guess my code for ape should be correct).

Thank you very much in advance and look forward to your reply!

Best,
Haixiao
